decisionsThatChangedSinceCp1.item: The buildable-figure gate is PROVENANCE, not arithmetic.
decisionsThatChangedSinceCp1.cp1Plan: Refuse the figure when the envelope atom's area disagrees with the sheet's own offset-ring area beyond a 2% tolerance.
decisionsThatChangedSinceCp1.whatHappened: That implementation broke three existing controls, one of them titled '(a) prints exactly ONE buildable figure and ONE consistent percent on every surface when the atom-backed (warm) and local figures differ'. Reading it showed the divergence is that control's METHOD: it sets the atom figure 4,000 sq ft away from the local derive precisely so a leak of the local number is unmistakable. A tolerance check would have destroyed the instrument that proves one figure prints per document.
decisionsThatChangedSinceCp1.resolution: The gate now fires on the setback values this export followed differing from the ones the persisted setback-rule atom carries — i.e. the envelope was derived from a source the sheet has stopped following. All three controls pass untouched. Two figures differing is P-159's method; two figures resting on different setback law is P-219's defect, and they are now distinguishable.

decisionsThatChangedSinceCp1.whatHappened: The ruled BDC chart could not serve as the export's fallback because R13 returns null for a Bastrop city district without a layer-23 per-parcel record. Amending it made three deliberate controls fail, one commented 'deliberately unchanged by P-154'.
decisionsThatChangedSinceCp1.resolution: Amendment reverted; the reasoning and this lane's supporting evidence are recorded in the code at the decision point, and the amendment is PROPOSED in the close rather than taken. In its place the resolver splits two concerns that R13 already distinguishes: SCALARS come from the rails (or an unretired atom, or honest absence) under every routing rule including R13, while the CITATION comes from `getSetbackTable`, the direct lookup R13 explicitly leaves open for 'edition/citation lookup'. The cost is that a Bastrop city parcel whose reader read fails now honest-absents its setback layer rather than falling back to a ruled number — no fabricated dimension, and not the repealed one either.

decisionsThatChangedSinceCp1.item: The situs fix was built, measured, and REVERTED.
decisionsThatChangedSinceCp1.whatHappened: The live PDF prints 'Address — UNAVAILABLE No addressed record on file for this parcel', so the export hands labelEdgesFromRoads a null situs while the parcel_record situsAddress rail carries '1109 PECAN ST'. The working hypothesis was that this is why the export produced no side_corner edge. It was wired to the record this lane already reads, then tested: labelEdgesFromRoads was run against this parcel's real ring and its three attaching OSM ways (15113894 Pecan Street, 1387340776, 1180352037, geometry pulled live from the OSM API 2026-09-15) both WITH and WITHOUT the situs, and returned the IDENTICAL role set both times — side_corner, front, side, side, rear.
decisionsThatChangedSinceCp1.resolution: The hypothesis was wrong and the change is reverted. Supplying a situs strengthens the front-edge basis product-wide, which can move the front edge on parcels nobody measured, in P-218's subject area, for no benefit to the parcel this row is about. The finding, the one-line fix and the measurement are recorded at the decision point in resolve-situs-for-export.ts and routed to P-218.

decisionsThatChangedSinceCp1.item: A fail-open in this lane's own code, caught by its own fixture.

Ungated, that hands ANY parcel stamped 'SF-1' with no jurisdiction key Bastrop's SF-1 numbers.
decisionsThatChangedSinceCp1.resolution: Gated on the parcel actually being in Bastrop County (FIPS 48021), with a regression test asserting both directions: a Travis County SF-1 parcel does not get Bastrop's ordinance cited over its numbers, and a Bastrop one does.
